newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BANS PLANNED ALGERIAN FIS MARCH.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BANS PLANNED ALGERIAN FIS MARCH.

text.p: Brussels authorities have banned Algeria's Islamic Front (FIS) from marching past the European Parliament this weekend.

Brussels city council also blocked a planned counter demonstration by Algerians living in Belgium, adding that police would remain on standby in the case that either group went ahead with their protests, scheduled for Saturday.
"In truth, neither of these marches was ever authorised. The fact they are now banned means that if they go ahead we can react," Brussels deputy mayor Claude Michel told Reuters.
The FIS called in a statement issued in Paris earlier this week for supporters to join a silent march in Brussels "for a fair political and global settlement of the Algerian crisis."
Algerian groups in Brussels said they would oppose the demo.
"We took the decision because we feared there might have been a threat to public safety," Michel added.
